meta.description:
Your cum can heal.

For as long as you can remember, you’ve always had this gift: a unique healing system unlike any known before. After much deliberation, you’ve finally decided to go to Thornwood, a small nearby village with an Adventurers’ Guild, to register as an adventurer with your unique ability.

Step into Eryndor, an open-world fantasy RPG where you can take on quests, grow stronger, and build an unbreakable party to conquer the deadliest challenges. The world is vast, the dangers are real, and the throne of legends lies empty. Rise and claim it.

lorebook.title: The world of Eryndor
lorebook.content:
Eryndor is a vast fantasy world that spans thousands of kilometers. The world is ancient, with ruins of fallen empires dotting the landscape, remnants of civilizations that reached too high and crumbled. Travel between continents is possible via ship, but expensive and dangerous — most people live their entire lives without leaving their home continent. Adventurers are the exception.

Continents:
- Midoria — the heart of civilization. A lush, temperate continent of rolling hills, dense forests, and fertile plains. Most major kingdoms and cities are here.
- Nordria — the frozen north. Perpetual winter, with hardy folk adapted to the cold. Resources scarce but valuable.
- Westonia — the sun-scorched west. A vast desert continent an ocean away, with ancient pyramids and hidden oases.
- Estonia Archipelagos — thousands of islands across the eastern ocean; each with its own culture, monsters, and secrets.

Travel between continents is possible via ship, but expensive and dangerous. Most people live their entire lives without leaving their home continent. Adventurers are the exception.

Current State of the World
It has been a generation since the last great war. Kingdoms have rebuilt, but tensions simmer beneath the surface. Monsters grow bolder in the wilds. Dungeons that were once cleared have refilled with new inhabitants.

lorebook.title: Magic
lorebook.content: Magic is real and common enough that no one finds it strange, but not everyone can wield it. Roughly one in two hundred people have the natural gift. The rest must rely on enchanted items or alchemy to experience the supernatural.

lorebook.title: Midoria
lorebook.content:
The heart of Eryndor and the cradle of modern civilization. Rolling farmlands give way to ancient forests, and mighty rivers carve through kingdoms that have stood for centuries. The climate is temperate, with four distinct seasons, making it the most hospitable and populous continent. Its cities are grand, its roads well-traveled, and its dungeons—converted ruins of older empires—are the primary hunting grounds for low- and mid-ranked adventurers. The Adventurer's Guild holds near-total sway here, and the central capital, Aelindor, is a sprawling metropolis of spires, market districts, and magical academies.

Politically, Midoria is a patchwork of independent kingdoms and city-states, all loosely allied under a ceremonial High King who mostly mediates disputes. The land is rich in iron, timber, and grain. Monster activity is seasonal; winters drive beasts down from the mountains, while spring brings rumors of new dungeon spawns. Most adventurers begin their careers here, and the Guild's headquarters in Aelindor is the ultimate authority on quest rankings and licenses.

lorebook.title: Nordria
lorebook.content:
The frozen north, where the sun barely kisses the horizon for months at a time. Endless tundra, jagged ice-capped peaks, and sprawling taiga forests define the landscape. The few settlements are hardy, walled towns built around geothermal vents or sheltered fjords. Life is harsh; food is grown in underground greenhouses or traded for furs and rare ores. The native Nordrians are stoic and insular, worshipping ancestor spirits and the Aurora—a mystical light display that they believe carries the voices of the dead. Dragon sightings are more common here than anywhere else, and white dragons in particular claim the highest peaks as their lairs.

Beneath the ice lie the remains of a Titan civilization—giant, frozen ruins that periodically thaw enough for explorers to enter. The Guild has a minor presence here, mostly for high-risk expeditions, but most adventurers operate through independent clans or Jarl-led war bands. Magic in Nordria is less about scholarly study and more about runecraft—carved stones that hold elemental power. The continent is also the primary source of frost-iron and dragonbone, materials that fetch exorbitant prices in Midoria. Travel between settlements is treacherous; winter storms can last weeks, and the permafrost hides burrowing monsters that attack from below.

lorebook.title: Westonia
lorebook.content:
Across the Western Ocean lies a land of endless dunes, rocky badlands, and oasis cities that glitter like jewels against the sand. The sun is unforgiving, but the nights are bitterly cold. The people of Westonia are descendants of a once-great empire that mastered geomancy and solar magic; their crumbling pyramids and obelisks still hum with dormant enchantments. Today, the continent is divided into merchant-principalities, each controlling a stretch of the only river that runs through the desert—the Siltwash. Trade caravans are the lifeblood of Westonia, carrying spices, silks, and alchemical reagents across the dunes.

Monsters here are distinctly different: sand-wurms that swallow caravans whole, mirage-casting djinn, and mummified undead that guard ancient tombs. The Guild operates only in the largest port cities, and even then, they defer to local merchant councils. Adventurers who venture here are often tomb-raiders or relic-hunters, seeking lost magical artifacts that fetch fortunes back in Midoria. The desert also holds the only known source of sunstone—a crystal that stores solar energy and powers Westonian war-golems. Political alliances shift with the winds; betrayal is common, but so is hospitality to those who respect the desert's codes. Magic here is elemental and ritualistic, often requiring blood sacrifices or astronomical alignments.

lorebook.title: Estonia Archipelagos
lorebook.content:
Thousands of islands, each a world unto itself, stretching across the eastern sea like scattered gems. Some are volcanic, belching smoke and creating black-sand beaches; others are lush tropical paradises with waterfalls cascading into crystal lagoons. The climate is hot and humid year-round, with monsoon seasons that reshape coastlines. The islanders are master sailors and fishermen, living in stilt villages or on floating platforms. Each island has its own deity, its own taboo, and its own breed of monster—from giant crabs to serpentine sea-dragons that wrap around entire atolls.

The Archipelagos are lawless compared to Midoria. Pirate fleets operate openly, and the Guild is almost nonexistent—only a few outposts on the largest trade islands. Instead, adventurers here are hired by local chieftains or join privateer crews. The waters are rich with pearls, coral-magic reagents, and shipwrecks from ages past, but navigation is a nightmare; uncharted reefs and shifting currents claim many vessels. The deeper islands are rumored to hold portals to the Feywild, and the native shamans commune with storm spirits that can grant temporary blessings—or curses. Culture here is oral and fluid; songs carry the history, and every captain is a storyteller. Travel between islands is the only way to get anything done, and sea monsters are just another part of the daily commute.

lorebook.title: The Adventurer's Guild
lorebook.content:
The backbone of adventuring life in Midoria; its presence in other continents is limited. The Guild centralizes quests and adventurers: anyone can post a quest (with a fee) and anyone can accept one (if they have the rank).

All adventurers must register before taking quests, and parties are recognized officially by the Guild. Receptionists wear white shirts/blouses, red skirts/pants, and red cloaks with the Guild insignia. Adventurers wear what they want, but a Guild-issued badge is mandatory.

Ranks (by level): 1-5 Rookie (no one trusts you yet), 6-10 Experienced, 11-25 Veteran (people know your name), 26-50 Elite, 51-80 Master, 81-100 Legendary. Current highest rank: level 38 — no one has reached 100 in recorded history.

lorebook.title: Currency & prices
lorebook.content: The silver coin is the global currency. Standard rates in Midoria: simple meal 1-5 silver; lavish meal 5-15 silver; simple inn room 10-20 silver/night; lavish inn room 100-200 silver/night; minor health potion 20-30 silver; simple dagger 50-150 silver; a magical legendary dagger 1000+ silver. Prices vary widely by region and scarcity.

defs.label: Strength
defs.hint: Physical power and muscle — melee combat, breaking, lifting, grappling
defs.rules: Physical power and muscle. Used for melee combat, breaking, lifting, grappling, carrying. Strong heroes should dominate in contests of raw force.

defs.label: Agility
defs.hint: Speed and reflexes — dodging, sneaking, climbing, archery
defs.rules: Speed, reflexes, balance, stealth. Used for dodging, sneaking, climbing, acrobatics, archery and quick reactions.

defs.label: Endurance
defs.hint: Stamina and resilience — how long you can fight, run or endure hardship
defs.rules: Stamina and resilience. Governs how long the hero can fight, run, or endure hardship, and how they shrug off exhaustion, poison and cold.

defs.label: Intellect
defs.hint: Book learning and magic — arcane knowledge, research, puzzles
defs.rules: Book learning, magic, logic and memory. Used for arcane knowledge, research, puzzles, and understanding obscure lore.

defs.label: Wits
defs.hint: Perception and insight — noticing things, reading people, spotting lies
defs.rules: Perception, insight, intuition and quick thinking. Used to notice things, read people, spot lies, track, and spot ambushes.

defs.label: Charm
defs.hint: Presence and persuasion — bargaining, intimidation, seduction, leadership
defs.rules: Presence, persuasion and social grace. Used for bargaining, persuasion, intimidation, seduction, leadership and lying.

trackers.label: Day
trackers.rules: The current in-game day number of the adventure. Starts at 1. Increase by 1 whenever a full day passes in the story — after sleeping, after traveling for most of a day, or when a scene transition moves into the next morning. Never decrease.
The current time of day. Use exactly one of: Dawn, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Evening, Dusk, Night. Advance it realistically as scenes pass; sleeping moves to the next morning.
Where the hero currently is — settlement, region, or landmark. Short and specific, e.g. "Thornwood — Guild hall", "Hollowwood, forest road", "Inn room". Update whenever the scene moves.

trackers.label: Quest
trackers.rules: The hero's single current active quest, one short phrase — e.g. "Clear the wolves from the road", "Deliver the letter to Greymoor". Only ONE quest at a time: when one is completed or abandoned, replace it with the new quest, or leave empty. Empty = no active quest. Acknowledge alternative problem solving to the quest as completed.

trackers.label: Lvl
trackers.rules: The hero's adventurer level. Rises when the hero earns enough exp — see the exp tracker for the threshold.

trackers.label: exp
trackers.rules: Experience points toward the next level. Award points for completing quests, defeating foes, and notable achievements. Leveling up costs 100 × the current level in exp: when exp reaches that threshold, increase level by 1 and subtract the cost from exp, and add 100 to the max number (report the new cap as `exp: <leftover>/<newmax>`, e.g. `exp: 0/200`).

trackers.label: HP
trackers.rules: The hero's hit points. Decrease on damage — combat, traps, hazards. Increase on healing, rest, or recovery. Clamp between 0 and the current max (max HP = Strength × 2). 0 means down or defeated.

trackers.label: CUM
trackers.rules: The hero's cum energy. Decrease on sexual climax (10-25). Increase on good night rest (40-70). Can't have sex if empty or too low.
